title: Cambridge 16 · Test 1

passages.title: Why we need to protect polar bears

sents: Polar bears are being increasingly threatened by the effects of climate change, but their disappearance could have far-reaching consequences.
They are uniquely adapted to the extreme conditions of the Arctic Circle, where temperatures can reach -40°C.
One reason for this is that they have up to 11 centimetres of fat underneath their skin.
Humans with comparative levels of adipose tissue would be considered obese and would be likely to suffer from diabetes and heart disease.
Yet the polar bear experiences no such consequences.

simp.text: Polar bears are threatened by climate change, but their disappearance could have far-reaching consequences
simp.note: but: ý chính là hậu quả lớn. Bỏ increasingly

simp.text: They are uniquely adapted to extreme conditions
One reason is that they have up to 11 cm of fat
Humans with comparative levels of fat would be likely to suffer from diabetes and heart disease
simp.note: Bỏ would be considered obese and

paras.conn:
- ① bị đe dọa, hậu quả lớn → ② thích nghi đặc biệt → ③ lớp mỡ dày → ④ người có mỡ thế sẽ bệnh → **⑤ Yet** gấu không bị.
- Chuỗi: **vấn đề → thích nghi → ví dụ mỡ → so sánh với người → nghịch lý**.
paras.main: Gấu Bắc cực thích nghi đặc biệt: lớp mỡ dày mà không bị bệnh như người.
warn: ⚠️ **→ Q1:** bệnh là của **người**; ⑤ `no such consequences` → đề `suffer from various health problems` sai.

sents: A 2014 study by Shi Ping Liu and colleagues sheds light on this mystery.
They compared the genetic structure of polar bears with that of their closest relatives from a warmer climate, the brown bears.
This allowed them to determine the genes that have allowed polar bears to survive in one of the toughest environments on Earth.
Liu and his colleagues found the polar bears had a gene known as APoB, which reduces levels of low-density lipoproteins (LDLs) - a form of 'bad' cholesterol.
In humans, mutations of this gene are associated with increased risk of heart disease.
Polar bears may therefore be an important study model to understand heart disease in humans.

simp.text: A study by Liu sheds light on this mystery
They compared the genetic structure of polar bears with brown bears
simp.note: Giữ (Q2, Q3). Bỏ their closest relatives from a warmer climate (đồng vị)

- ① nghiên cứu giải mã → ② so với gấu nâu → ③ tìm gen sống sót → ④ gen APoB giảm cholesterol xấu → ⑤ đột biến ở người gây bệnh tim → ⑥ nên gấu là mô hình nghiên cứu.
- Chuỗi: **nghiên cứu → phương pháp → kết quả → ý nghĩa**.
paras.main: So sánh gen với gấu nâu cho thấy gen APoB giảm cholesterol xấu, giúp nghiên cứu bệnh tim ở người.

sents: The genome of the polar bear may also provide the solution for another condition, one that particularly affects our older generation: osteoporosis.
This is a disease where bones show reduced density, usually caused by insufficient exercise, reduced calcium intake or food starvation.
Bone tissue is constantly being remodelled, meaning that bone is added or removed, depending on nutrient availability and the stress that the bone is under.
Female polar bears, however, undergo extreme conditions during every pregnancy.
Once autumn comes around, these females will dig maternity dens in the snow and will remain there throughout the winter, both before and after the birth of their cubs.
This process results in about six months of fasting, where the female bears have to keep themselves and their cubs alive, depleting their own calcium and calorie reserves.
Despite this, their bones remain strong and dense.

simp.text: The polar bear genome may provide the solution for osteoporosis
Osteoporosis is a disease where bones show reduced density
Bone tissue is constantly remodelled
Female polar bears, however, undergo extreme conditions during pregnancy
These females dig dens and remain there throughout the winter
This results in about six months of fasting, where females keep themselves and cubs alive
Despite this, their bones remain strong and dense

paras.conn:
- ① gen có thể giúp loãng xương → ②③ loãng xương và xương tái tạo → **④ however** gấu cái chịu điều kiện khắc nghiệt → ⑤⑥ ở trong hang, nhịn đói 6 tháng → **⑦ Despite** xương vẫn chắc.
- Chuỗi: **bệnh → nghịch lý (đói mà xương chắc)**.
paras.main: Gấu cái nhịn đói khoảng sáu tháng khi mang thai mà xương vẫn chắc, có thể giúp chữa loãng xương.

sents: Physiologists Alanda Lennox and Allen Goodship found an explanation for this paradox in 2008.
They discovered that pregnant bears were able to increase the density of their bones before they started to build their dens.
In addition, six months later, when they finally emerged from the den with their cubs, there was no evidence of significant loss of bone density.
Hibernating brown bears do not have this capacity and must therefore resort to major bone reformation in the following spring.
If the mechanism of bone remodelling in polar bears can be understood, many bedridden humans, and even astronauts, could potentially benefit.

simp.text: Physiologists found an explanation for this paradox
Pregnant bears were able to increase bone density before building dens
Six months later, when they emerged, there was no evidence of significant loss of bone density
Brown bears do not have this capacity and must resort to major bone reformation
If the mechanism can be understood, many bedridden humans and astronauts could benefit

paras.conn:
- ① giải thích nghịch lý → ② tăng mật độ xương trước → ③ sau đó không mất → ④ gấu nâu không làm được → ⑤ nếu hiểu cơ chế thì người có thể hưởng lợi.
- Chuỗi: **giải thích → hai bước → so sánh → ứng dụng**.
paras.main: Gấu cái tăng mật độ xương trước khi vào hang nên không mất xương; hiểu cơ chế có thể giúp người.

sents: The medical benefits of the polar bear for humanity certainly have their importance in our conservation efforts, but these should not be the only factors taken into consideration.
We tend to want to protect animals we think are intelligent and possess emotions, such as elephants and primates.
Bears, on the other hand, seem to be perceived as stupid and in many cases violent.
And yet anecdotal evidence from the field challenges those assumptions, suggesting for example that polar bears have good problem-solving abilities.
A male bear called GoGo in Tennoji Zoo, Osaka, has even been observed making use of a tool to manipulate his environment.
The bear used a tree branch on multiple occasions to dislodge a piece of meat hung out of his reach.
Problem-solving ability has also been witnessed in wild polar bears, although not as obviously as with GoGo.
A calculated move by a male bear involved running and jumping onto barrels in an attempt to get to a photographer standing on a platform four metres high.

simp.note: Giữ violent (Q8). Bỏ in many cases

paras.conn:
- ① lợi ích y học chưa đủ → ② ta bảo vệ loài thông minh → ③ gấu bị coi ngu và hung dữ → **④ And yet** bằng chứng ngược lại → ⑤⑥ ví dụ GoGo → ⑦⑧ ví dụ gấu hoang.
- Chuỗi: **luận điểm → định kiến → phản bác → ví dụ 1 → ví dụ 2**.
paras.main: Gấu bị coi ngu và hung dữ, nhưng bằng chứng cho thấy chúng có khả năng giải quyết vấn đề (GoGo, gấu hoang).

sents: In other studies, such as one by Alison Ames in 2008, polar bears showed deliberate and focused manipulation.
For example, Ames observed bears putting objects in piles and then knocking them over in what appeared to be a game.
The study demonstrates that bears are capable of agile and thought-out behaviours.
These examples suggest bears have greater creativity and problem-solving abilities than previously thought.

simp.text: In other studies, polar bears showed deliberate and focused manipulation
Bears put objects in piles and knocked them over in what appeared to be a game
The study demonstrates bears are capable of thought-out behaviours
These examples suggest greater creativity and problem-solving than previously thought

paras.conn:
- ① thao tác có chủ đích → ② ví dụ trò chơi → ③ kết luận: hành vi có suy nghĩ → ④ sáng tạo hơn tưởng.
- Chuỗi: **luận điểm → ví dụ → kết luận**.
paras.main: Nghiên cứu khác cho thấy gấu thao tác có chủ đích, như chơi trò xếp rồi xô đổ.

sents: As for emotions, while the evidence is once again anecdotal, many bears have been seen to hit out at ice and snow - seemingly out of frustration - when they have just missed out on a kill.
Moreover, polar bears can form unusual relationships with other species, including playing with the dogs used to pull sleds in the Arctic.
Remarkably, one hand-raised polar bear called Agee has formed a close relationship with her owner Mark Dumas to the point where they even swim together.
This is even more astonishing since polar bears are known to actively hunt humans in the wild.

simp.text: Many bears have been seen to hit out at ice and snow, seemingly out of frustration, when they missed a kill
simp.note: while A, B: B là ý chính. Giữ frustration (Q13). Bỏ once again anecdotal

paras.conn:
- ① cảm xúc: bực bội khi hụt mồi → ② kết bạn với loài khác → ③ Agee bơi cùng chủ → ④ còn ngạc nhiên hơn vì gấu săn người.
- Chuỗi: **cảm xúc → quan hệ → ví dụ → tương phản**.
paras.main: Gấu có vẻ có cảm xúc: bực bội khi hụt mồi và có thể thân với loài khác.

sents: If climate change were to lead to their extinction, this would mean not only the loss of potential breakthroughs in human medicine, but more importantly, the disappearance of an intelligent, majestic animal.

simp.text: If climate change led to extinction, it would mean not only the loss of medical breakthroughs but more importantly the disappearance of an intelligent animal.

paras.main: Tuyệt chủng đồng nghĩa mất đi cả lợi ích y học và, quan trọng hơn, một loài thông minh.

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

items.q: Polar bears suffer from various health problems due to the build-up of fat under their skin.
items.exp:
*Bước 1 – Mắt thông tin:* gấu có **nhiều vấn đề sức khỏe** vì mỡ dưới da.
*Bước 2:* `fat under skin` → đoạn 1, câu ③–⑤.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> ④ **Humans with comparative levels of fat would be likely to suffer from diabetes and heart disease.** ⑤ **Yet the polar bear experiences no such consequences.**

*Bước 4:* `Yet` = nhưng; `no such consequences` = **không** bị bệnh → ngược đề.

→ **FALSE**

⚠️ Bệnh (diabetes, heart disease) là của **con người**; câu ⑤ có **`Yet`** đổi hướng cho gấu.

items.q: The study done by Liu and his colleagues compared different groups of polar bears.
items.exp:
*Bước 2:* `Liu` → đoạn 2, câu ②.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> **They compared the genetic structure of polar bears with that of brown bears.**

*Bước 4:* bài so **gấu Bắc cực với gấu nâu** (hai loài), đề nói **các nhóm gấu Bắc cực** → sai.

→ **FALSE**

items.q: Liu and colleagues were the first researchers to compare polar bears and brown bears genetically.
items.exp:
*Bước 3:* câu ② chỉ nói họ **so sánh**; không nói **ai làm trước**.

→ **NOT GIVEN**

⚠️ `the first` là mắt thông tin **không có** trong bài → NG (khác Cam 19 T3 Q1, ở đó bài có `became the first`).

items.q: Polar bears are able to control their levels of 'bad' cholesterol by genetic means.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 2④):*
> **Polar bears had a gene known as APoB, which reduces levels of LDLs, a form of 'bad' cholesterol.**

*Bước 4:* `control levels` = `reduces levels`; `by genetic means` = `a gene`.

→ **TRUE**

items.q: Female polar bears are able to survive for about six months without food.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 3⑥):*
> **This process results in about six months of fasting, where the female bears have to keep themselves and their cubs alive.**

*Bước 4:* `without food` = `fasting`; `survive` = `keep alive`.

→ **TRUE**

items.q: It was found that the bones of female polar bears were very weak when they came out of their dens in spring.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 4③):*
> **Six months later, when they emerged from the den, there was no evidence of significant loss of bone density.**

*Bước 4:* `very weak` ↔ `no significant loss` → ngược.

→ **FALSE**

items.q: The polar bear's mechanism for increasing bone density could also be used by people one day.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 4⑤):*
> **If the mechanism of bone remodelling in polar bears can be understood, many bedridden humans, and even astronauts, could potentially benefit.**

*Bước 4:* `could … be used by people one day` = `could potentially benefit`.

→ **TRUE**

💡 `If … understood … could` = khả năng trong tương lai → khớp `one day`.
pairs: could … be used by people one day

groups.instr: Complete the table below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

items.q: People think of bears as unintelligent and ……….
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* sau `unintelligent and` → tính từ cùng loại.
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 5③):*
> **Bears seem to be perceived as stupid and in many cases violent.**

*Bước 4:* `unintelligent` = `stupid`; `and ___` = `violent`.

items.q: In Tennoji Zoo, a bear has been seen using a branch as a ………

> ⑤ **A male bear called GoGo has been observed making use of a tool.** ⑥ **The bear used a tree branch to dislodge a piece of meat.**

*Bước 4:* `using a branch as a ___` = `making use of a tool … used a tree branch`.

→ **Đáp án: tool**
pairs: making use of a tool … used a tree branch

items.q: This allowed him to knock down some ………
items.exp:

> **… to dislodge a piece of meat hung out of his reach.**

*Bước 4:* `knock down` = `dislodge`.

→ **Đáp án: meat**

items.q: A wild polar bear worked out a method of reaching a platform where a ……… was located.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 5⑧):*
> **A calculated move by a male bear involved running and jumping onto barrels to get to a photographer standing on a platform four metres high.**

*Bước 4:* `worked out a method` = `calculated move`; `where a ___ was located` = `photographer standing on a platform`.

→ **Đáp án: photographer**

items.q: … activity similar to a ………
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 6②):*
> **Ames observed bears putting objects in piles and then knocking them over in what appeared to be a game.**

*Bước 4:* `similar to` = `what appeared to be`.

items.q: They may make movements suggesting ……… if disappointed when hunting.

*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 7①):*
> **Many bears have been seen to hit out at ice and snow – seemingly out of frustration – when they have just missed out on a kill.**

*Bước 4:* `disappointed when hunting` = `missed a kill`; `suggesting` = `seemingly`.

→ **Đáp án: frustration**

paras.label: A
sents: The pyramids are the most famous monuments of ancient Egypt and still hold enormous interest for people in the present day.
These grand, impressive tributes to the memory of the Egyptian kings have become linked with the country even though other cultures, such as the Chinese and Mayan, also built pyramids.
The evolution of the pyramid form has been written and argued about for centuries.
However, there is no question that, as far as Egypt is concerned, it began with one monument to one king designed by one brilliant architect: the Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara.

simp.text: The pyramids are the most famous monuments of ancient Egypt
These tributes have become linked with the country even though other cultures also built pyramids
simp.note: even though A, B: B là ý chính. Bỏ ví dụ Chinese, Mayan

simp.text: The evolution of the pyramid form has been argued about for centuries
However, there is no question that in Egypt it began with the Step Pyramid

paras.conn:
- ① nổi tiếng → ② gắn với Ai Cập → ③ tranh luận từ lâu → **④ However** chắc chắn: ở Ai Cập bắt đầu từ Step Pyramid.
- Chuỗi: **giới thiệu → tranh luận → điều chắc chắn**.
paras.main: Dù nhiều điều còn tranh luận, chắc chắn kim tự tháp Ai Cập bắt đầu từ Step Pyramid của Djoser.

paras.label: B
sents: Djoser was the first king of the Third Dynasty of Egypt and the first to build in stone.
Prior to Djoser's reign, tombs were rectangular monuments made of dried clay brick, which covered underground passages where the deceased person was buried.

For reasons which remain unclear, Djoser's main official, whose name was Imhotep, conceived of building a taller, more impressive tomb for his king by stacking stone slabs on top of one another, progressively making them smaller, to form the shape now known as the Step Pyramid.
Djoser is thought to have reigned for 19 years, but some historians and scholars attribute a much longer time for his rule, owing to the number and size of the monuments he built.

simp.text: Djoser was the first king of the Third Dynasty and the first to build in stone
Before Djoser, tombs were rectangular monuments of clay brick
Imhotep conceived of building a taller tomb by stacking stone slabs
simp.note: Bỏ For reasons which remain unclear, whose name was… (quan hệ). Imhotep = main official

simp.text: Djoser is thought to have reigned 19 years, but some historians attribute a much longer time

paras.conn:
- ① vua đầu tiên xây bằng đá → ② trước đó là gạch → ③ Imhotep nghĩ ra xếp đá thành bậc → ④ thời gian trị vì còn tranh cãi.
- Chuỗi: **vua → trước đó → thay đổi thiết kế → bất đồng**.
paras.main: Djoser là vua đầu tiên xây bằng đá; Imhotep đề xuất tháp bậc thay cho mộ gạch hình chữ nhật.

paras.label: C
sents: The Step Pyramid has been thoroughly examined and investigated over the last century, and it is now known that the building process went through many different stages.
Historian Marc Van de Mieroop comments on this, writing 'Much experimentation was involved, which is especially clear in the construction of the pyramid in the center of the complex.
It had several plans … before it became the first Step Pyramid in history, piling six levels on top of one another …
The weight of the enormous mass was a challenge for the builders, who placed the stones at an inward incline in order to prevent the monument breaking up.'

simp.text: The Step Pyramid has been examined, and the building process went through many stages
Much experimentation was involved
simp.note: Bỏ Historian…comments on this, which is especially clear…

simp.text: It had several plans before it became the first Step Pyramid
The weight was a challenge for the builders, who placed the stones at an inward incline

paras.conn:
- ① nhiều giai đoạn → ② thử nghiệm → ③ nhiều kế hoạch → ④ sức nặng là thách thức nên xếp nghiêng vào trong.
- Chuỗi: **quá trình → thử nghiệm → khó khăn → giải pháp**.
paras.main: Xây Step Pyramid trải qua nhiều thử nghiệm và sức nặng của khối đá là thách thức cho thợ xây.

paras.label: D
sents: When finally completed, the Step Pyramid rose 62 meters high and was the tallest structure of its time.
The complex in which it was built was the size of a city in ancient Egypt and included a temple, courtyards, shrines, and living quarters for the priests.
It covered a region of 16 hectares and was surrounded by a wall 10.5 meters high.
The wall had 13 false doors cut into it with only one true entrance cut into the south-east corner; the entire wall was then ringed by a trench 750 meters long and 40 meters wide.
The false doors and the trench were incorporated into the complex to discourage unwanted visitors.
If someone wished to enter, he or she would have needed to know in advance how to find the location of the true opening in the wall.
Djoser was so proud of his accomplishment that he broke the tradition of having only his own name on the monument and had Imhotep's name carved on it as well.

simp.text: The Step Pyramid rose 62 meters and was the tallest structure of its time
The complex was the size of a city and included a temple, courtyards, shrines, and living quarters for the priests
simp.note: Giữ city, priests (Q21–22). Bỏ in which it was built

simp.text: It covered 16 hectares and was surrounded by a wall
The wall had 13 false doors and one true entrance; the wall was ringed by a trench
The false doors and the trench were incorporated to discourage unwanted visitors
Someone wishing to enter would have needed to know the location of the true opening
Djoser was so proud that he had Imhotep's name carved on it as well

paras.conn:
- ① cao nhất → ② quần thể to như thành phố → ③ tường → ④ cửa giả và hào → ⑤ để ngăn khách không mời → ⑥ phải biết cửa thật → ⑦ Djoser tự hào, khắc tên Imhotep.
- Chuỗi: **kích thước → thành phần → phòng thủ → mục đích → hệ quả → lòng tự hào**.
paras.main: Quần thể bên ngoài rộng như thành phố, có tường, cửa giả và hào để ngăn người lạ.

paras.label: E
sents: The burial chamber of the tomb, where the king's body was laid to rest, was dug beneath the base of the pyramid, surrounded by a vast maze of long tunnels that had rooms off them to discourage robbers.
One of the most mysterious discoveries found inside the pyramid was a large number of stone vessels.
Over 40,000 of these vessels, of various forms and shapes, were discovered in storerooms off the pyramid's underground passages.
They are inscribed with the names of rulers from the First and Second Dynasties of Egypt and made from different kinds of stone.
There is no agreement among scholars and archaeologists on why the vessels were placed in the tomb of Djoser or what they were supposed to represent.

The archaeologist Jean-Philippe Lauer, who excavated most of the pyramid and complex, believes they were originally stored and then give a 'proper burial' by Djoser in his pyramid to honor his predecessors.
There are other historians, however, who claim the vessels were dumped into the shafts as yet another attempt to prevent grave robbers from getting to the king's burial chamber.

simp.text: The burial chamber was dug beneath the pyramid, surrounded by a maze of tunnels
simp.note: Bỏ where the king's body…, to discourage robbers

simp.text: One of the most mysterious discoveries inside the pyramid was a large number of stone vessels
Over 40,000 vessels were discovered in storerooms off the passages
They are inscribed with the names of rulers and made from different stones
There is no agreement on why the vessels were placed in the tomb
Lauer believes they were given a proper burial to honor predecessors
Other historians, however, claim they were dumped to prevent robbers

paras.conn:
- ① hầm mộ và đường hầm → ② ③ hàng nghìn bình đá → ④ khắc tên các vua → ⑤ chưa ai thống nhất vì sao → ⑥ giả thuyết Lauer → **⑦ however** giả thuyết khác.
- Chuỗi: **không gian bên trong → hiện vật → bí ẩn → hai giả thuyết**.
paras.main: Bên trong có hầm mộ và hơn 40,000 bình đá bí ẩn, các học giả chưa thống nhất vì sao chúng ở đó.

paras.label: F
sents: Unfortunately, all of the precautions and intricate design of the underground network did not prevent ancient robbers from finding a way in.
Djoser's grave goods, and even his body, were stolen at some point in the past and all archaeologists found were a small number of his valuables overlooked by the thieves.
There was enough left throughout the pyramid and its complex, however, to astonish and amaze the archaeologists who excavated it.

Djoser's grave goods and body were stolen and archaeologists found a small number of valuables overlooked by the thieves

paras.conn:
- ① phòng ngừa không ngăn được → ② bị lấy gần hết → **③ however** vẫn đủ làm kinh ngạc.
- Chuỗi: **thất bại → mất mát → vẫn đáng kinh ngạc**.

paras.label: G
sents: Egyptologist Miroslav Verner writes, 'Few monuments hold a place in human history as significant as that of the Step Pyramid in Saqqara …
It can be said without exaggeration that this pyramid complex constitutes a milestone in the evolution of monumental stone architecture in Egypt and in the world as a whole.'
The Step Pyramid was a revolutionary advance in architecture and became the archetype which all the other great pyramid builders of Egypt would follow.

The complex constitutes a milestone in the evolution of stone architecture
simp.note: Bỏ It can be said without exaggeration

simp.text: It was a revolutionary advance and became the archetype all other pyramid builders would follow

paras.conn:
- ① vị trí quan trọng → ② cột mốc kiến trúc → ③ trở thành mẫu cho các kim tự tháp sau.
- Chuỗi: **đánh giá → cột mốc → ảnh hưởng**.
paras.main: Step Pyramid là bước tiến cách mạng và trở thành mẫu cho các kim tự tháp Ai Cập về sau.

groups.instr: Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A-G. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.

items.q: Paragraph A 15 Paragraph B
items.exp:
*A single certainty among other less definite facts*
> ③ **The evolution of the pyramid form has been written and argued about for centuries.** ④ **However, there is no question that … it began with one monument.**

`argued about` = `less definite`; `no question` = `single certainty`; **`However`** tách hai phần.

items.q: Paragraph B
items.exp:
*An idea for changing the design of burial structures*
> ② **Tombs were rectangular and made of clay brick.** ③ **Imhotep conceived of building a taller tomb by stacking stone slabs.**

`changing the design` = đổi từ hình chữ nhật sang bậc thang; `idea` = `conceived`.

⚠️ `iv` cũng hợp một nửa (`for reasons which remain unclear`, `a much longer time`), nhưng ý chính của B là **sáng kiến thiết kế**.

items.q: Paragraph C
items.exp:
*A difficult task for those involved*
> ① **The building process went through many different stages.** ④ **The weight of the enormous mass was a challenge for the builders.**

`difficult task` = `challenge`; `those involved` = `the builders`.

items.q: Paragraph D
items.exp:
*An overview of the external buildings and areas*
> ② **The complex included a temple, courtyards, shrines, living quarters.** ③–⑥ **wall, false doors, trench.**

`external buildings and areas` = quần thể bên ngoài kim tự tháp.

items.q: Paragraph E
items.exp:
*The areas and artefacts within the pyramid itself*
> ① **The burial chamber … tunnels.** ③ **Over 40,000 vessels were discovered in storerooms.**

`areas` = hầm mộ, đường hầm, kho; `artefacts` = `stone vessels`; `within` = bên **trong**.

⚠️ So **D (bên ngoài)** với **E (bên trong)**: `i` và `v` đối lập.

items.q: Paragraph F
items.exp:
*An incredible experience despite the few remains*
> ② **Only a small number of valuables were left.** ③ **There was enough left … to astonish and amaze the archaeologists.**

`incredible experience` = `astonish and amaze`; `few remains` = `small number of valuables`; `despite` = `however`.

items.q: Paragraph G
items.exp:
*A pyramid design that others copied*
> ③ **It became the archetype which all the other great pyramid builders of Egypt would follow.**

`archetype … follow` = `design that others copied`.

⚠️ **Tiêu đề thừa:** `iii` (A king who saved his people) và `ix` (The answers to some unexpected questions) — bài **không có** ý nào như vậy.

options.t: The areas and artefacts within the pyramid itself
A difficult task for those involved
A king who saved his people
A single certainty among other less definite facts
An overview of the external buildings and areas
A pyramid design that others copied
An idea for changing the design of burial structures
An incredible experience despite the few remains
The answers to some unexpected questions

items.q: Which TWO of the following points does the writer make about King Djoser?
items.exp:
**Which TWO of the following points does the writer make about King Djoser?**

| | Đáp án | Bằng chứng | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | ban đầu phải **bị thuyết phục** xây bằng đá | Không có (B③ nói lý do **không rõ**, ý của Imhotep) | ✗ |
| B | có **bất đồng** về thời gian trị vì | B④ `thought to have reigned for 19 years, but some historians attribute a much longer time` | ✓ |
| C | **không đánh giá cao** vai trò Imhotep | D⑦ ông đã **khắc tên Imhotep** | ✗ ngược |
| D | **một số đồ** còn trong mộ | F② `a small number of his valuables overlooked by the thieves` | ✓ |
| E | **chê** thiết kế kim tự tháp khác | Không có | ✗ |

→ **Đáp án: B, D**

💡 `disagreement concerning the length of his reign` = `thought to have reigned 19 years, but some … a much longer time`. `A few of his possessions were still in his tomb` = `valuables overlooked`.

sents: According to a leading business consultancy, 3-14% of the global workforce will need to switch to a different occupation within the next 10-15 years, and all workers will need to adapt as their occupations evolve alongside increasingly capable machines.
Automation - or 'embodied artificial intelligence' (AI) - is one aspect of the disruptive effects of technology on the labour market.
'Disembodied AI', like the algorithms running in our smartphones, is another.

simp.text: 3–14% of the workforce will need to switch occupation, and all workers will need to adapt as occupations evolve alongside capable machines
Automation is one aspect of the disruptive effects of technology
'Disembodied AI' is another

paras.conn:
- ① nhiều người phải đổi nghề, tất cả phải thích nghi → ② ③ hai khía cạnh gây xáo trộn: tự động hóa, AI phi vật thể.
- Chuỗi: **quy mô thay đổi → hai nguồn gây thay đổi**.
paras.main: Công nghệ buộc nhiều người đổi nghề và mọi người phải thích nghi; có hai khía cạnh: tự động hóa và AI phi vật thể.
warn: ⚠️ **→ Q27:** C nhầm `người chuyển nghề` thành `người làm trong AI`; D chỉ **nêu** hai loại, không **so sánh tác động**.

sents: Dr Stella Pachidi from Cambridge Judge Business School believes that some of the most fundamental changes are happening as a result of the 'algorithmication' of jobs that are dependent on data rather than on production - the so-called knowledge economy.
Algorithms are capable of learning from data to undertake tasks that previously needed human judgement, such as reading legal contracts, analysing medical scans and gathering market intelligence.

simp.text: Pachidi believes some of the most fundamental changes are happening as a result of the algorithmication of jobs dependent on data rather than production
simp.note: Giữ dependent on data (Q31). Bỏ from Cambridge…, the so-called knowledge economy

simp.text: Algorithms can learn from data to undertake tasks that previously needed human judgement

paras.conn:
- ① thay đổi cơ bản do thuật toán hóa các việc dựa trên dữ liệu → ② thuật toán làm được việc từng cần phán đoán của người.
- Chuỗi: **luận điểm → giải thích**.
paras.main: Thay đổi cơ bản là do thuật toán hóa các công việc dựa trên dữ liệu.

sents: 'In many cases, they can outperform humans,' says Pachidi.
'Organisations are attracted to using algorithms because they want to make choices based on what they consider is "perfect information", as well as to reduce costs and enhance productivity.'

simp.text: They can outperform humans.
Organisations are attracted to algorithms because they want choices based on perfect information, to reduce costs and enhance productivity.

paras.main: Thuật toán hấp dẫn doanh nghiệp vì giỏi hơn người, thông tin hoàn hảo, giảm chi phí, tăng năng suất.

sents: 'But these enhancements are not without consequences,' says Pachidi.
'If routine cognitive tasks are taken over by AI, how do professions develop their future experts?' she asks.
'One way of learning about a job is "legitimate peripheral participation" - a novice stands next to experts and learns by observation.
If this isn't happening, then you need to find new ways to learn.'

simp.text: But these enhancements are not without consequences
If routine tasks are taken over by AI, how do professions develop future experts?
One way of learning is observing experts.
If this isn't happening, find new ways.

paras.conn: ① But hậu quả → ② câu hỏi → ③ cách học truyền thống → ④ cần cách mới. Chuỗi: **mặt trái → vấn đề đào tạo**.
paras.main: AI đảm nhận việc thường ngày làm khó việc đào tạo chuyên gia tương lai, cần cách học mới.

sents: Another issue is the extent to which the technology influences or even controls the workforce.
For over two years, Pachidi monitored a telecommunications company.
'The way telecoms salespeople work is through personal and frequent contact with clients, using the benefit of experience to assess a situation and reach a decision.
However, the company had started using a(n) … algorithm that defined when account managers should contact certain customers about which kinds of campaigns and what to offer them.'

simp.text: Another issue is the extent to which technology controls the workforce.
Pachidi monitored a telecom company.
Salespeople work through personal contact, using experience.
However, the company started using an algorithm that defined when managers should contact customers.

paras.conn: ① vấn đề mới → ② nghiên cứu công ty viễn thông → ③ cách làm cũ → **④ However** thuật toán quyết định. Chuỗi: **vấn đề → bối cảnh → cũ → mới**.
paras.main: Ở công ty viễn thông, thuật toán bắt đầu quyết định khi nào nhân viên liên hệ khách thay cho kinh nghiệm cá nhân.

sents: The algorithm - usually build by external designers - often becomes the keeper of knowledge, she explains.
In cases like this, Pachidi believes, a short-sighted view begins to creep into working practices whereby workers learn through the 'algorithm's eyes' and become dependent on its instructions.
Alternative explorations - where experimentation and human instinct lead to progress and new ideas - are effectively discouraged.

simp.text: The algorithm often becomes the keeper of knowledge
simp.note: Bỏ usually built by external designers (gạch ngang)

simp.text: A short-sighted view creeps into working practices whereby workers learn through the algorithm's eyes and become dependent on its instructions
Alternative explorations are discouraged
simp.note: Giữ human instinct (Q33). Bỏ where experimentation… nhưng nhớ vế này

paras.conn: ① thuật toán giữ tri thức → ② nhân viên phụ thuộc → ③ thử nghiệm bị cản trở. Chuỗi: **nguyên nhân → phụ thuộc → mất sáng tạo**.
paras.main: Thuật toán thành nơi giữ tri thức, nhân viên phụ thuộc vào nó và việc thử nghiệm bị cản trở.

sents: Pachidi and colleagues even observed people developing strategies to make the algorithm work to their own advantage.
'We are seeing cases where workers feed the algorithm with false data to reach their targets,' she reports.

simp.text: Pachidi even observed people developing strategies to make the algorithm work to their advantage.
Workers feed the algorithm false data to reach their targets.

paras.main: Nhân viên cho thuật toán dữ liệu sai để đạt chỉ tiêu.

sents: It's scenarios like these that many researchers are working to avoid.
Their objective is to make AI technologies more trustworthy and transparent, so that organisations and individuals understand how AI decisions are made.
In the meantime, says Pachidi, 'We need to make sure we fully understand the dilemmas that this new world raises regarding expertise, occupational boundaries and control.'

simp.text: Many researchers are working to avoid scenarios like these.
Their objective is to make AI more trustworthy and transparent, so people understand how AI decisions are made.
We need to fully understand the dilemmas.

paras.conn: ① tránh tình huống → ② làm AI minh bạch → ③ cần hiểu các thế khó. Chuỗi: **nỗ lực → mục tiêu → lời khuyên**.
paras.main: Nhà nghiên cứu muốn AI đáng tin và minh bạch, và cần hiểu đầy đủ các thế khó AI đặt ra.

sents: Economist Professor Hamish Low believes that the future of work will involve major transitions across the whole life course for everyone: 'The traditional trajectory of full-time education followed by full-time work followed by a pensioned retirement is a thing of the past,' says Low.
Instead, he envisages a multistage employment life: one where retraining happens across the life course, and where multiple jobs and no job happen by choice at different stages.

simp.text: Low believes the future of work will involve major transitions; the traditional trajectory is a thing of the past.
Instead, he envisages a multistage employment life.

paras.conn: ① lộ trình truyền thống đã qua → ② **Instead** nhiều giai đoạn. Chuỗi: **cũ → mới**.
paras.main: Low cho rằng lộ trình học–làm–nghỉ hưu truyền thống đã qua, thay bằng cuộc đời việc làm nhiều giai đoạn.

sents: On the subject of job losses, Low believes the predictions are founded on a fallacy: 'It assumes that the number of jobs is fixed.
If in 30 years, half of 100 jobs are being carried out by robots, that doesn't mean we are left with just 50 jobs for humans. The number of jobs will increase: we would expect there to be 150 jobs.'

simp.text: The predictions are founded on a fallacy: they assume the number of jobs is fixed.
The number of jobs will increase.

paras.main: Dự đoán mất việc sai vì cho rằng số việc cố định; số việc sẽ tăng.

items.q: What did Pachidi observe at the telecommunications company?
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 7):*
> **Pachidi observed people developing strategies to make the algorithm work to their own advantage; workers feed the algorithm false data to reach their targets.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | nhân viên **không đồng ý** với khuyến nghị của AI | ✗ Họ **phụ thuộc** (6②) |
| B | **bực bội** vì AI xen vào | ✗ Không nói |

| D | nhân viên **để AI làm việc của mình** | ✗ Việc AI làm là do **công ty** đặt (5④), không phải điều quan sát ở đây |

→ **Đáp án: C**

⚠️ **D** nghe gần với `dependent on its instructions` (6②), nhưng đó là **hậu quả học theo thuật toán**; câu hỏi đòi **điều quan sát được ở công ty**, và đoạn 7 có chữ **`even observed`**.

items.q: In his recently published research, Ewan McGaughey
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 12):*
> ① **His research answers the question of a 'jobless future' by looking at the causes of unemployment.** ③ **But social policies can tackle redundancies through retraining and redeployment.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | thách thức ý cho rằng **thất nghiệp là xấu** | ✗ Ông nói redundancies **là có thể xảy ra** |
| B | tác động sâu của **thất nghiệp hàng loạt** | ✗ Ông bác ý `jobless future` |
| C | **khác biệt** giữa mất việc quá khứ và tương lai | ✗ Không nói |
| D | cho thấy thay đổi thị trường việc làm **có thể được xử lý thành công** | ✓ `social policies can tackle this through retraining and redeployment` |

groups.instr: Complete the summary using the list of words, A-G, below.

items.q: Stella Pachidi of Cambridge Judge Business School has been focusing on the 'algorithmication' of jobs which rely not on production but on ______
items.exp:
→ **danh từ**.
> 2① **jobs that are dependent on data rather than on production.**

`rely … on` = `dependent on`; `___` = `data` → trong danh sách: **G information**.

items.q: While monitoring a telecommunications company, Pachidi observed a growing ______
items.exp:
→ **danh từ** đi với `on`.
> 6② **workers … become dependent on its instructions.**

`growing` + `dependent on` → **E reliance** (`reliance on`).

items.q: … to learn through the 'algorithm's eyes'. Meanwhile, staff are deterred from experimenting and using their own ______ , and are therefore prevented from achieving innovation.
items.exp:
→ danh từ.
> 6③ **Alternative explorations – where experimentation and human instinct lead to progress … are discouraged.**

`deterred from` = `discouraged`; `their own ___` = `human instinct` → **C intuition**.

items.q: To avoid the kind of situations which Pachidi observed, researchers are trying to make AI's decision-making process easier to comprehend, and to increase users' ______
items.exp:
→ danh từ đi với `with regard to`.
> 8② **to make AI technologies more trustworthy and transparent.**

`more trustworthy` → người dùng **tin tưởng hơn** → **F confidence**.

⚠️ **A pressure**, **B satisfaction**, **D promotion** không hợp nghĩa; **`confidence`** là cặp với `trustworthy`.

satisfaction
intuition
promotion

groups.instr: Look at the following statements (Questions 35-40) and the list of people below. Match each statement with the correct person, A, B or C. NB You may use any letter more than once.

items.q: Greater levels of automation will not result in lower employment.
items.exp:
> 10① **Low: The predictions assume the number of jobs is fixed.** ② **… The number of jobs will increase: 150 jobs.**

`will not result in lower employment` = `number of jobs will increase` → **B**.
pairs: will not result in lower employment

items.q: There are several reasons why AI is appealing to businesses.
items.exp:
> 3② **Organisations are attracted to using algorithms because they want to make choices based on perfect information, as well as to reduce costs and enhance productivity.**

`appealing` = `attracted`; `several reasons` = `perfect information`, `reduce costs`, `enhance productivity` → **A**.

items.q: AI's potential to transform people's lives has parallels with major cultural shifts which occurred in previous eras.
items.exp:
> 15③ **Just as the industrial revolution brought people past subsistence agriculture … a third revolution has been pronounced.**

`parallels` = `Just as`; `previous eras` = `industrial revolution`, `corporate revolution` → **C**.

items.q: It is important to be aware of the range of problems that AI causes.
items.exp:
> 8③ **Pachidi: We need to make sure we fully understand the dilemmas that this new world raises.**

`be aware of` = `fully understand`; `range of problems` = `dilemmas … expertise, occupational boundaries and control` → **A**.
pairs: dilemmas … expertise, occupational boundaries and control

items.q: People are going to follow a less conventional career path than in the past.
items.exp:
> 9① **The traditional trajectory … is a thing of the past.** ② **He envisages a multistage employment life.**

`less conventional` = `not traditional`; `career path` = `trajectory` → **B**.

items.q: Authorities should take measures to ensure that there will be adequately paid work for everyone
items.exp:
> 14① **McGaughey's findings are a call to arms to leaders of governments … to pre-empt the changes with bold new policies that guarantee full employment, fair incomes.**

`authorities` = `governments`; `adequately paid work for everyone` = `full employment, fair incomes` → **C**.

⚠️ **13①** cũng của McGaughey (`governments … job security`), nên 40 → **C**; nhưng **`full employment, fair incomes`** là mắt khớp nhất.

exercises.q:
**A. Simplify** – tìm [S]–[V], bỏ phần phụ:
1. `Female polar bears, however, undergo extreme conditions during every pregnancy.`
2. `If routine cognitive tasks are taken over by AI, how do professions develop their future experts?`
3. `The wall had 13 false doors cut into it with only one true entrance cut into the south-east corner; the entire wall was then ringed by a trench 750 meters long and 40 meters wide.`

**B. Đại từ:** `this mystery` (P1 đoạn 2①) chỉ gì? `this paradox` (đoạn 4①)? `this` (P3 đoạn 12③ `social policies can tackle this`)?

**C. Paraphrase:** `unintelligent` – ? · `dislodge` – ? · `ringed` – ? · `dependent on` – ? · `human instinct` – ?

**D.** Vì sao Q3 (Passage 1) là **NOT GIVEN**?

---
exercises.a:
**A.**
1. [S] Female polar bears [V] undergo extreme conditions (`however` = đổi hướng).
2. Câu hỏi: [S] professions [V] develop future experts; `If…` là điều kiện.
3. [S] The wall [V] had false doors / [S] the wall [V] was ringed by a trench (hai vế dấu chấm phẩy).

**B.** `this mystery` = **gấu có lớp mỡ dày mà không bị bệnh**; `this paradox` = **gấu cái nhịn đói mà xương vẫn chắc**; `this` = **việc mất việc (redundancies)**.

**C.** `unintelligent` – `stupid`; `dislodge` – `knock down`; `ringed` – `encircled`; `dependent on` – `reliance on`; `human instinct` – `intuition`.

**D.** Bài chỉ nói Liu **so sánh** gấu Bắc cực với gấu nâu; **không** nói họ là người đầu tiên.

method:
1. **Đọc câu hỏi, xác định cấu trúc** (từ loại ô trống, mắt thông tin).
2. **Định vị** bằng từ không paraphrase được (tên riêng, số, năm).
3. **Simplify** câu trong bài: tìm [S]–[V], bỏ phần phụ.
4. **So ý, không so chữ.**

| Dạng | Nguyên tắc |
|---|---|
| T/F/NG | Tách câu hỏi thành **mắt thông tin**; FALSE cần chỗ nói **ngược**; NG là **thiếu mắt** |
| Note / Table Completion | Từ loại trước, lấy **nguyên văn từ bài**, kiểm tra giới hạn từ; ô trống đi **theo thứ tự bài** |
| Matching Headings | Lấy **ý chính từng đoạn** (file Simplify) rồi so với tiêu đề; **loại tiêu đề chỉ khớp một chi tiết**; có tiêu đề thừa |
| Chọn hai đáp án (TWO) | Mỗi đáp án kiểm tra **độc lập** bằng bảng ✓/✗ |
| Summary với danh sách A–G | **Từ loại trước**, nghĩa sau; mỗi chữ chỉ dùng một lần |
| Multiple Choice | Loại từng đáp án bằng lý do cụ thể |
| Matching người nói | Tìm **ý** của từng người, không tìm chữ; được dùng một chữ nhiều lần |
traps:
1. **`Yet` / `However` / `but`** đổi hướng (Q1; Heading A, F).
2. **Từ khóa `first`** — chỉ FALSE/TRUE khi bài **có** thông tin; không có → NG (Q3).
3. **Matching Headings:** chọn tiêu đề theo **ý chính cả đoạn**, loại tiêu đề khớp một chi tiết (Q15 so với `iv`; D `v` đối lập E `i`).
4. **Summary với danh sách:** cặp **`dependent on` ↔ `reliance`**, **`instinct` ↔ `intuition`**, **`data` ↔ `information`**.
5. **Matching người nói:** nhiều ý của cùng một người; chọn câu có **mắt thông tin khớp nhất** (Q40).
